posts.text: BREAKING: Global physical gold-backed ETFs posted +$3.5 billion in inflows last week, the largest weekly intake since February 2026. This also marks the 6th consecutive weekly inflow, the longest streak since January. Over this 6-week period, ETFs have attracted +$10.0 billion in inflows. This is equivalent to +72.2 tons of gold, bringing ETF holdings up to 4,114 tons, the highest since May. European funds led last week’s demand at +$2.3 billion, followed by North America at +$1.1 billion, and Asia at +$200 million. Global demand for gold is acclerating sharply.

posts.text: The United States did not force the world to adopt an unbacked Eurodollar as global money. The world willingly chose that on its own. And not wanting to have a currency mismatch between its liabilities and its revenues/assets is why the rest of the world holds USD reserves. And THAT is the eurodollar trap. As such, despite what JD Vance or anyone else thinks or prefers, transitioning away from the USD as the reserve currency of the world will not be a smooth or nonvolatile event for the rest of the world.
